name: Bera
title: King of Sodom
summary: Bera was the king of Sodom during Abraham's time. He is best known for his role in the war between the four kings and the five kings in the Valley of Siddim, and for his meeting with Abram after Abram had rescued Lot and the other captives. Bera offered Abram the spoils of war, but Abram refused so as not to owe anything to the king of Sodom.

keyEvents.title: The War in the Valley of Siddim
keyEvents.description: Bera and four other kings in the Jordan Plain revolted against Kedorlaomer after twelve years as vassals. They met Kedorlaomer and his allies in the Valley of Siddim, but suffered defeat.

keyEvents.title: Defeat and Flight
keyEvents.description: Bera and the king of Gomorrah fled when their army was defeated. Many fell into asphalt pits in the Valley of Siddim, and the rest fled to the mountains.

keyEvents.title: Sodom Plundered and Lot Taken Captive
keyEvents.description: After the victory, Kedorlaomer and his allies plundered Sodom and Gomorrah and took all their goods and food, including Lot, Abram's relative who lived in Sodom.

keyEvents.title: Abram rescues the captives
keyEvents.description: When Abram heard that Lot had been taken captive, he gathered 318 trained men and pursued the enemy as far as Dan and then to Hobah, north of Damascus. He defeated them and freed all the captives and recovered the goods.

keyEvents.title: Bera meets Abram after the victory
keyEvents.description: After Abram's victory, Bera, king of Sodom, went out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh (the King's Valley). Bera asked Abram to return the people but let him keep the goods himself.

keyEvents.title: Abram declines Bera's offer
keyEvents.description: Abram declined Bera's offer and swore by the Lord, God Most High, that he would not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap from the king of Sodom, so that Bera could not say he had made Abram rich.
